assertions.name: cross_anchor_spread_matches_15th_power_propagation
assertions.unit: relative spread of A/ℏ_q^15 between the proton and muon anchors
assertions.source: Route A: |target_p − target_m|/target_p from the two 50-dps anchors. Route B: 15·Δq/(q(q−1)), the first-order propagation of Δq through ℏ=(q−1)/q and the 15th power. Tolerance 5e-12 sits just above the second-order term 120·(Δℏ/ℏ)² = 1.32e-12 and ~3e6 below the quantity itself.

assertions.name: step3_proton_anchor_tier
assertions.source: Proton-anchor tier: MISS (Step 2 found NEAR-1PCT here)

description: Step 3 of PR #1772 Chain 4 — cross-anchor validation of Step 2's NEAR-1PCT candidate cocharge_(1,1,1,1) = 6 at q_proton. The candidate is anchor-INDEPENDENT (combinatorial), but the target A / ℏ_q^15 differs between q_proton and q_muon by 1.573e-6 relative. Verdict: WIDE MISS — candidate refuted at cross-anchor.

data.verdict: WIDE MISS — candidate refuted at cross-anchor

caveats: step3_proton_anchor_tier is RED and belongs red: cocharge_(1,1,1,1)=6 against the canonical target 2.0717 gives ratio 2.896, tier MISS, while the assertion encodes Step 2's NEAR-1PCT claim. The script's own else-branch says the same thing in prose — Step 2's NEAR-1PCT was a bug artifact from a non-canonical ℏ_q. Left failing rather than rewritten green; it is the refutation, recorded.

The else-branch used to print 'a wrong target ~6.47'. A/ℏ^15 at Step 2's hard-coded ℏ=0.0922502 is 6.0496, not 6.47 — the 6.47 was never computed by anything. Now printed live from RESIDUE_A so it cannot drift again; the ~2.07 in the same sentence was correct.
